text: What you find worth liking sits right on the person they are trying to be. Your Venus and their Sun occupy the same ground, so your taste and their identity are not two separate subjects here. You do not have to work out whether you approve of them. The approval is already in place, aimed at the center of them rather than at some quality out on the edge. For them this comes close to being enjoyed for existing. Most regard has conditions attached, and yours does not seem to. They walk in as themselves and you are already pleased, so the effort they usually spend making a case for who they are is not needed in your company. People rarely forget who did that for them. It also means your opinion weighs more in this relationship than it does anywhere else in your life. A cool afternoon from you reads to them as a ruling on their character, not on the afternoon. Your own side of the exchange is easy to miss because it is so pleasant. Their vitality gives your sense of value something living to attach to. Taste on its own can stay a matter of objects and arrangements. Here it fastens onto a person with a direction, and your liking gets pulled along behind their aims. You may notice that what you consider worth your time and money has quietly reorganized itself around what serves them. That can be generous. It can also be a slow way of losing the thread of your own preferences. There is a flattery problem built into a contact this close. Praise costs you nothing, so you may hand it over automatically, and automatic praise stops carrying any news. They then have no way to tell whether your pleasure is real, and you have no reliable way to raise a complaint, because a complaint from you lands harder than you meant it to. Pairs with this contact often go years without one plain critical sentence passing between them, and both of them call that peace. Money, gifts, and comfort tend to move along this line early, in whatever form the relationship allows. You want to give them things, or improve their surroundings, or talk them up to other people. It is rarely calculated. It is what happens when one person's taste and another person's self-regard stand in the same place. Whether the two of you are family, colleagues, or friends of long standing, this makes you an unusually good mirror and an unreliable one. Keeping it honest means liking things that have nothing to do with them, and saying the mild true thing early, while it is still mild. Regard that survives a small correction is worth more to them than regard that has never been tested, and it stays more interesting to you.

This contact does not switch itself on. Your Venus sits at a friendly angle to their Sun, which puts appreciation within reach without putting any of it in motion. The two of you can be cordial for years and never once use what is available here, and nothing will look wrong while that happens. Used, it works like this. You are able to be specific about them. You notice what they are good at, and you can say so in a way that embarrasses neither of you. Praise from you is not sticky. It arrives, it is accurate, and it asks for nothing back, which is exactly why they can take it. People who are hard to compliment often find they can accept one from you. What comes back is a steadying of your own preferences. Their sense of purpose is a fixed point, and it is easier to know what you value when something definite is standing nearby to be valued or declined. Around them you tend to make clearer decisions about whose company is worth an evening and what you are willing to pay for. They are not choosing for you. Their clarity gives yours something to push against. At work this makes you a good advocate for them. You can describe what they do to a third person better than they can describe it themselves, because you are not tangled in their pride while doing it. In a friendship it shows up as low, dependable goodwill: you are glad when they turn up, and you are not keeping score. The limit deserves stating plainly, since sextiles get sold as small trines. Nothing here will hold weight you have not deliberately put on it. Unused, this angle leaves you as someone who thinks well of them and never mentions it, and leaves them without the evidence. If the relationship comes under strain, there is no reflex to fall back on. There is a route, and routes only help the people who take them. A quieter failure runs alongside. Because appreciating them is easy for you, it can stay cheap. You pay the compliment, they enjoy it, nothing changes for either of you, and both of you start treating the exchange as manners. Manners are not nothing. They are also not what this could be. Growth here is unglamorous and specific. Name the thing you admire while they can still hear it as news. Ask for something you actually want from them instead of waiting to be offered it. Let them do you a favor now and then, since one-way warmth stays shallow no matter how sincere it is. Each real use makes the next one easier, and left alone the angle keeps sitting there, polite and mostly unspent.

Your sense of what is agreeable keeps failing to confirm the thing they are proudest of. That is this square, stated flatly, and it happens without either of you deciding anything. They are being themselves at full volume. You are wincing slightly, or smoothing, or moving the conversation along, and they feel it land. From their side the difficulty is that your regard is precisely what would help, and it comes with a hesitation in it. You like a great deal about them. You do not like it at the moment they most want it liked. What reaches them is a small withholding, and since a Sun is not built to shrug that off, they usually push harder: more assertion, more display, more insistence that this is simply who they are. Which is the register your Venus finds excessive. The loop starts easily and is hard to see from inside. From your side, their self-assertion keeps crossing your sense of proportion. Something in how they take up space strikes you as more than the occasion called for. You rarely say this outright, because your instinct under friction is to keep the air pleasant, so it comes out sideways. A joke with a point on it. A compliment that lands slightly to the left of what they wanted. An evening arranged around your idea of a good time rather than theirs. Shared taste and shared spending are the obvious sites. What counts as a treat, how a room should look, which occasions deserve effort, whose friends are worth the trouble. None of those arguments is really about the object. Each is a small vote on whose values set the terms, and the votes keep going differently. There is genuine traction in this. A square will not let either position stay comfortable. You get pushed into saying what you value in plain words instead of expressing it through arrangements, which is harder than it sounds for anyone whose first language is atmosphere. They get pushed into learning that their way of being impressive is not universally impressive, and that a person can like them thoroughly and still not applaud on cue. Both of those are useful facts, and most people never receive them. Plenty of durable alliances run on exactly this grind. The square reports where two charts rub, and it reports nothing about what the two of you make of the rubbing. What changes over time, if you stay in it, is the sideways habit. You get quicker at naming the objection while it is still small. They get quicker at hearing an objection as a preference rather than as a review of their character. The friction stays. It gets cheaper to run.

Liking them takes nothing out of you. Your Venus trines their Sun, and the practical meaning is that your regard for this person runs with no maintenance at all. You are not managing an impression of them in your head. You do not have to talk yourself back into it after a bad week. Whatever they did on Tuesday, by Thursday you are glad they exist. They experience it as a room with no draft. Around you they are not being assessed. That is rarer than it sounds, since most people rate each other quietly and constantly, and anyone who has spent years being slightly too much or slightly not enough notices the absence at once. They tend to be more themselves in your company, and more willing to try things, because failing in front of you does not cost them your good opinion. You get something back that is easy to overlook. Their clarity about who they are is restful for your taste. You never have to construct a reason to enjoy them. Having one relationship that requires no calibration frees up a surprising amount of attention for everything else in your life. The honest limitation is that none of this asks anything of either of you. A trine has no appetite for difficulty. Your approval is not conditional, which means it also does not get revised, and an opinion that never gets revised is not really an opinion. You may find you have not updated your picture of them in years. If they are doing something you would object to in anyone else, this angle is perfectly willing to let it pass unmentioned for a decade. A second cost is quieter. Warmth this automatic tends to go unspoken. You assume they know, and they mostly do, so the particular compliment never gets made and the specific thanks never gets said. Then circumstances shift, and neither of you has any recent evidence to consult. Two things are worth separating, since this contact makes them easy to confuse. Being enjoyed and being understood are different achievements. You can like someone completely and know very little about what their days are actually made of. The trine hands over the first at no charge and does nothing whatever about the second. What the ease is good for is stamina. A person who has somewhere to be uncomplicatedly welcome attempts more elsewhere and recovers faster from the results. That is not a small thing to be for somebody, or to have. It simply does not do the other job, and nothing in the aspect will tell you which job you have been doing.

Across the width of the two charts, what you find valuable is looking straight at who they are. An opposition blends nothing. It sets two functions face to face, so you are unusually aware of them, and unusually aware of your own reaction to them. The first thing this produces is attraction of a specific kind. They tend to have, or simply to be, something you have wanted and have not managed to become. Confidence, perhaps. Or a directness about wanting things. Or the plain willingness to be the center of an occasion, which you can admire and find slightly rude at the same time. The pull is real, and it stays powered by the distance between you. The role it hands you is audience, and that is the part to watch. You appreciate them, you speak well of them, you notice what they are good at, and doing it is genuinely enjoyable. An appreciator can also slide into being scenery for the appreciated. You may find you know a great deal about their aims and can barely state your own, or that shared plans get built around their direction because yours was never put forward with the same force. What they meet in you is a person whose values do not automatically bend to their momentum. That is not always comfortable for them. Your sense of what is worth having, what is enough, when to stop and enjoy something, works as a live counterweight to a Sun that wants to keep going and be counted for it. They may hear that as a brake. Sometimes it is one. Often it is the only thing in the room asking what all the effort is for. So the argument, whatever it looks like from outside, runs along one line: whether the point is to get somewhere or to have a decent life while it happens. Both positions are defensible. Neither of you will win, because each is holding a real half. Oppositions complete as much as they confront, and this one has a clean version. You can take back some willingness to be central, to want a thing out loud without apologizing for the size of the wanting. They can take on some of your ability to enjoy what is already built instead of only the next thing. Neither transfer happens on its own, and each feels at first like a concession. Long stretches of this contact tend to leave a person more definite. Standing across from someone that unmistakable makes it hard to keep your own preferences vague, which is the useful thing that comes of never quite agreeing.

The kindness you hand out lands below the level of their opinion. Your Venus sits on their Moon, so what you enjoy giving reaches the part of them that reacts before it thinks. They do not decide to be comforted by you. They simply are, often within the first hour, and they may not be able to say why. You are good at this here without trying. The room you arrange, the food you choose, the tone you use when somebody is in a state: with this person those choices land accurately nearly every time. Elsewhere your taste is a matter of preference. With them it doubles as care, because what you find pleasant happens to be shaped like what settles them. Their side of the exchange gives you an immediate readout. Most people receive generosity politely and leave you guessing whether it worked. They have no such filter. Their mood changes in front of you, quickly and visibly, and before long you are steering by it. A readout that fast is hard not to obey. Steering by somebody else's comfort is habit-forming, and you can travel a long way down that road while calling it thoughtfulness. Two drifts are common. In the first you become the one who makes things nice, permanently, and your own needs never get raised, partly because raising them would disturb the pleasant thing you built. In the second they come to rely on your warmth the way people rely on the heating. Nobody thanks the heating. If your attention goes elsewhere for a month, they feel it as the weather turning rather than as a change in another person's life, and it can surface as a complaint that seems out of proportion. There is also the matter of what never gets said. When someone's moods answer this readily to your care, the temptation is to manage the mood instead of asking about the cause. A bad hour can be soothed rather than examined. Do that often enough and the two of you have a very comfortable relationship with a subject in it that has never once been named. A conjunction fuses, and fused warmth is strong whether or not anyone looks at it closely. What the contact guarantees is that you hold real influence over this person's inner weather, more than your ordinary behavior would predict, and that your own sense of value gets a fast and pleasant answer every time you use it here. Keeping it honest is mostly a matter of asking rather than supplying. Let them tell you what they need instead of arriving with it prepared, and state your own plainly at least sometimes. Comfort the two of you chose holds up better than comfort one of you administers.

Nothing here is compulsory, and that is the easiest thing to miss about it. The sextile your Venus makes to their Moon fits your way of showing regard to their way of needing comfort. It fits well enough to be useful and loosely enough that neither of you is obliged to do anything with it. The effect, on the days either of you draws on it, is small and dependable. You can be kind to them in a way that gets through. The gesture arrives at the right size, which matters more than it sounds, since most misfired care misfires on scale rather than on intent. You do not overwhelm them and you do not underdo it. They can accept something from you without feeling watched. They give you an easy read in return. Their moods are legible enough that you know when to bring a subject up and when to let the evening alone. You are rarely blindsided by them and rarely made to guess. Anyone who has spent time around a person whose weather is a puzzle knows how much energy that saves. In shared living, in an office, or in the friendship that runs on ordinary contact, this is a quiet asset. Small courtesies pass back and forth. Nobody feels handled. The bond has a low background level of comfort that neither of you had to negotiate for. The gap here is a feature of the angle, not a failing of either of you. A sextile does nothing unasked. You can hold this contact for years and never learn whether the two of you would be any good to each other in a genuinely bad week, because the aspect never forced the question and neither did you. It will not deepen by itself, and it will not stop the relationship from thinning into occasional contact that both of you keep calling closeness. There is a version of this that stays purely social. You are pleasant to them, they are easy around you, and both of you assume that means more than it does. Then something hard arrives and you find you have no practice at the other kind of conversation. Nothing broke. Nothing was ever built. What builds it is spending it deliberately, in the least impressive ways available. Turn up for the dull part of their week. Ask what they actually want instead of offering what is convenient to give. Accept care from them rather than only providing it, which is the harder half for most people who enjoy giving. The channel widens with use and only with use, and a small resource spent on purpose tends to outlast a large one nobody manages.

You keep offering the nice version of care to somebody whose comfort is built out of other material. Your Venus squares their Moon, so your sense of what is pleasant and their reflex for what is safe sit at an angle that does not settle into agreement. The gesture that misses is the signature of this contact. You arrange the evening and it is the wrong evening. You bring the good thing when they wanted the plain thing, or wanted nothing, or wanted you there with no plan attached. Nothing you did was careless. Your care was pitched to a register their comfort does not receive on, and they can tell that effort went into it, which makes the mismatch harder for both of you to raise. From their side, your preferences can read as pressure to be presentable. Their Moon has days with no polish on them, needs that arrive with no justification, moods that are not attractive and are not going anywhere for a while. Beside a person with a strong sense of how things ought to feel, they may suspect that the unlovely version of themselves is inconvenient. Some of that is their own guardedness. Some of it is accurate. From your side, their moods keep declining what you offer, and a declined offer stings in a way that is hard to admit out loud. You may respond by trying harder in the same direction, since taste is what you have, and the second attempt lands no better than the first. Or you go cool. Withdrawing warmth is the move your Venus has available under strain, and it registers on their nervous system faster than any argument would. The productive part is that neither of you can leave this implied. A square keeps returning to the same ground until somebody speaks. You end up having to ask what they need, plainly, and to accept an answer that has nothing to do with what you would have wanted in their position. They end up having to say the unglamorous thing instead of radiating it and hoping. Pairs who manage that acquire specific working knowledge of each other, which comfortable pairs rarely bother to collect. Domestic detail is where it lives. How a shared space should look against how it should feel. What an occasion requires. Whether money goes to the pleasant thing or the practical one. How much fuss counts as attention rather than as noise. These are not trivial arguments dressed up as large ones. They are large arguments wearing small clothes. The mismatch does not go away, and it was never going to. What can change is the interval between the misfire and the conversation about it, and over the years that interval is most of the difference between a bond that grates and one that works.

Your regard reaches them in the register they actually feel things in, and it needs no adjustment on the way. Your Venus trines their Moon, which means your way of giving pleasure and their way of taking comfort were built compatible. You never learned how to be good to this person. You simply are, and they do not have to translate it. The ordinary evidence is dull and constant. They relax when you come in. Your presence lowers whatever they had raised. You choose well for them without asking, and when you do ask, the answer is never a surprise. Silence with them is not a problem to be solved. A whole category of effort that other relationships demand is absent from this one. They give you something back in a currency easy to overlook. Around them your generosity is uncomplicated. Nowhere in this bond do you have to calculate whether a kindness will be misread, resented, or converted into an obligation, so the giving stays enjoyable instead of turning into a job. People who like looking after others often end up doing it warily. Not here. Every trine carries the same weakness, and it is worth being exact about this one. Neither of you is put to any trouble here. Your warmth is never tested, so it is never proved. Their comfort is always available, so neither of you develops the skill of asking clearly for what you need. Years can pass in a thoroughly pleasant relationship where the difficult material lives somewhere else entirely, and both of you sincerely believe you are close. There is a particular way this goes quiet. Because pleasing them is easy, pleasing them stops being an event. Kindness turns into background. Neither of you says thank you, since thanks would feel strange for something so ordinary, and then the ordinary thing is doing important work that nobody has acknowledged in years. It is also possible to enjoy being someone's comfort a little too much and to let that stand in for being known by them. Comfort and knowledge are separate goods. This aspect supplies the first free of charge and has no opinion about the second. If you want more than the default, bring the contact something it was not designed for. Let them see you needing rather than providing. Raise the unpleasant subject in the comfortable room instead of carrying it elsewhere. The ease will hold it, which is the real gift here, and trying is the only way to find that out.

Your pleasures and their needs face each other from opposite ends of the wheel, near enough to stay constantly visible and far enough apart that neither one absorbs the other. You know what they require in order to feel safe. They know what you like. Neither piece of knowledge makes the difference any smaller. The pull is real. Their steadiness looks restful to you, particularly in the stretches when your own taste feels restless or expensive. Your capacity for enjoyment looks like an open window to them, especially from inside a life organized around the familiar. Each of you carries something the other left underdeveloped, and both of you notice it early. Then the roles set. You become the one with preferences and they become the one with requirements, and after a while nobody is playing both parts. Your suggestions start to sound to them like a demand to be somewhere other than home. Their needs start to sound to you like a bill arriving every time you propose something good. Both readings are caricatures, and they are the caricatures this angle offers first. What you do to them, specifically, is unsettle the boundary of what is enough. You show them that comfort is not the only measure, that a thing can be worth having because it is good rather than because it is familiar. That can be freeing. It can also feel like being told the life they built is small, especially on a day when the familiar is the only thing holding them together. What they do to you is put a floor under your enjoyment. Taste with nothing beneath it gets tiring, and somebody who knows how to make an ordinary week survivable is offering you something your Venus does not generate on its own. You may find you resist the offer. Being looked after in the plain domestic way can feel like a reduction to anyone whose instinct runs toward the elegant version. The clean use of an opposition is to take on the other half rather than to keep borrowing it. You build some ordinary comfort of your own instead of having it delivered. They develop some appetite of their own instead of tasting yours secondhand. Neither move is automatic, and both feel like ceding ground at the start. When that happens, the two of you stop being a supply arrangement and become two people who each got wider. When it does not, the line stays drawn and you keep having the same argument about a weekend. The aspect has nothing to say about which one you get. It only guarantees that you are looking straight at the thing you never developed, held by somebody who did.

Your sense of what is worth having settles on the way they think and talk. With your Venus on their Mercury, their mind is not a neutral object to you. You find their phrasing pleasing, their curiosity attractive, the particular way they sort a problem enjoyable to watch. That is the fusion here, and it does something to them almost at once. People are rarely told that their thinking is a pleasure. They are told it is right or wrong, useful or beside the point. Your regard lands where they keep no defenses, and the result is that they talk more freely around you than around nearly anyone. Half-formed ideas come out. Jokes get made that would not survive a tougher room. If they have spent a life being corrected, your company is where the correcting stops. What makes that valuable is also what makes it unreliable. Because your liking attaches to how they put things, you can end up valuing the phrasing above the content. A well-made sentence from them will carry a bad plan straight past your judgment. You notice this mostly in retrospect, having agreed to something on Tuesday that made no sense by Friday, and the honest account is that you were charmed rather than persuaded. Their side of the exchange reaches your preferences directly. What they say about a thing changes how much you like it. A dry remark about something you were quietly enjoying can take the shine off it, and they will not know they did that, because to them it was only a remark. Worth telling them at some point. Otherwise they keep spending a currency they do not know they hold. Then there is the flattery loop. You praise how they think, they perform how they think, you praise the performance. The talk between you gets more delightful and less informative. Neither of you is being false, exactly. The conversation has simply started optimizing for the wrong thing. Practical life goes quickly here. Shopping, planning, choosing between options, describing a room or a person: the two of you settle these fast, because you know what you want and they can name it. Whatever the relationship is, this makes you a good pair to put a decision in front of. What keeps it interesting is a little friction in the talk. Disagree with them about something you actually care about, and let it be slightly awkward. A mind that is only ever enjoyed does not get sharper, and a taste that is always narrated by somebody else stops being yours. The pleasure in this contact survives some roughness. It does not survive going unused.

An open line runs between what you value and how they think, and neither of you is standing on it. A sextile makes something possible without making it happen. Here, what is possible is putting your preferences into a form their mind can work with, and getting back a description of them that is sharper than the one you started with. Try it and the mechanism shows. You say you would rather not go, and they ask the question that finds the actual reason. You describe something you liked, badly, and they hand you the word you were missing. Your taste tends to arrive as a whole impression with nothing underneath it. Their thinking is good at the underneath, and it is available at a comfortable distance, so you can take it without feeling analyzed. What goes the other way is easy for both of you to miss. Your regard makes their information welcome. Plenty of people who think clearly are used to being tolerated rather than enjoyed, and around you their explanations are received as good company instead of as a lecture. They talk more, and better, and they notice the difference even if they never mention it. The angle keeps its own temperature. Disagreements between you stay at the level of topics. You can tell them their reasoning has missed something, or hear the same in return, without the room changing. That is not harmony. It means whatever trouble the two of you have comes from elsewhere, and this piece of the exchange keeps offering a way back to a civil conversation. The weakness is the weakness of anything optional. This contact will sit unused for as long as you leave it. Pleasant conversation is its resting state, and pleasant conversation is a place two people can park for years. Nothing here obliges you to say the difficult sentence, and nothing penalizes you for skipping it. Spending it is simple and slightly effortful. It means asking what they think about something you had already settled by feel, or saying out loud why you like a thing in more words than seem necessary, or letting them talk you through a choice instead of handing over the finished preference. Each of those widens the line a little. What the aspect provides is a route between your liking and their understanding. Whether the two of you ever walk it is not settled by the geometry.

They have reasons for everything, including the things you simply like. Your Venus squares their Mercury, so your preferences and their sorting keep approaching the same subject from angles that will not line up. The recurring scene is a small one. You say you want something, or that something is lovely, or that you would rather not. They ask why. The question is not usually hostile, and it does not usually help, because the honest answer is that you know without knowing why. Pressed, you produce a reason that is not the real one. They take it apart, correctly, and you end up further from what you meant than when you started. What their thinking does to your taste, over time, is make it defensive. You begin preparing a case before saying what you want, or you stop saying it and arrange for it quietly instead. Neither habit is good for you. A preference that has to be justified before it can be voiced tends to shrink down to whatever can be justified. What your Venus does to them is more provoking than you might guess. You keep declining to argue. You go pleasant, or you move the subject along, or you concede the point in words while the preference stays exactly where it was. To a mind that runs on stated reasons, that looks like evasion, and it can make them press harder or sharper, which is the last thing that would help. Money, taste, and how a shared decision gets made are the usual arenas. They can explain why the sensible option is sensible. You cannot explain why it is joyless, only that it is, and the two of you have no common currency for settling it. Both frustrations are legitimate. Neither of you is being unreasonable in your own terms. The traction is that this square makes each of you learn the other's language, badly and slowly, which is the only way anybody learns one. You pick up enough of the explaining habit to state what you value in terms somebody else can act on, and that skill travels well outside this relationship. They pick up the fact that some things are known before they are argued, and that a person is not being difficult when they cannot supply footnotes for a preference. What tends to happen with time is that you get faster at saying which of your likes are open to discussion and which are simply not, and they get faster at hearing that distinction as information rather than as a wall.

They can put words to what you like, and the words are usually right. Your Venus trines their Mercury, so your sense of value and their way of thinking reach the same conclusions from different directions, comfortably enough that neither of you notices it happening. In conversation this shows up as being understood without effort. You describe a half-feeling about a person or a plan and they finish it accurately. Your taste, which is not naturally verbal, borrows their fluency. You end up more articulate about what you want in their company than you manage anywhere else, and getting there costs you nothing. They enjoy the exchange in their own way. Ideas are received warmly here rather than merely processed, and their thinking is treated as something to appreciate instead of something to check. Around you their talk gets easier, less guarded, a little more graceful than usual. That is a real service, and neither of you is likely to mention it. Agreement this smooth never gets audited, and that is the cost of it. You are inclined to accept their account of what you think, because it sounds better than your own version, and it usually is better phrased. Better phrased is not the same as true. Over the years you can end up with a description of your own preferences that came mostly from them, and no memory of having handed the job across. A second soft spot sits beside it. Because talking is pleasant here, both of you steer toward the pleasant part of any subject. Plans get agreed while the mood is good and the details get skipped, and the details are where the disagreement was hiding. The conversation ran so easily that neither of you noticed nothing had actually been settled. The smoothness is still worth having. This is a durable working channel. Hard news travels well between you, an awkward request does not curdle, and you can raise money or plans or a difficult third person without either of you bracing first. None of that has to be maintained, and none of it wears out on its own. It is worth pointing at something that matters rather than letting it hum. The fluency will not run out, and it will not deepen on its own either. What you get from spending it is a habit of settling real questions with this person, so that when something serious lands, the two of you already have a method and do not have to invent one under pressure.

You know what you want. They know what is the case. Your Venus and their Mercury sit at opposite ends of a line, so those two kinds of knowing stay permanently in view of each other, and neither one converts into the other. The visible version is a conversation that keeps not finishing. They lay out the considerations. You listen, and at some point you say what you would prefer, which is a sentence with no argument inside it. To them that arrives as the discussion being cut off rather than concluded. To you, their explaining feels like a way of postponing the part where somebody finally says what they want. Each of you is holding a real half. Preference with no information gets people into avoidable trouble, and the trouble is usually expensive. Information with no preference produces excellent analysis of a choice nobody ever makes. You have watched them stall in front of options that were all fine. They have watched you commit in three seconds on grounds you could not name afterward. What their Mercury does to you, at its best, is give your liking a structure. You come away knowing not only that you want it but what it is you want, which makes it possible to ask for. At its worst it makes you feel processed. A preference being examined out loud can stop feeling like yours, and if you have ever gone quiet in the middle of explaining why you love something, this angle is often the reason. What your Venus does to them is put a value on the end of the reasoning. Their thinking finds it easy to keep going and hard to stop, and stopping requires a judgment about what is worth having, which is not their department. You supply the stopping point. That is a service, and it can also feel to them like being overruled by something they are not allowed to inspect. The failure mode is the polarized version, where you become the one with feelings and they become the one with facts and both of you settle in. You stop offering reasons because reasons get examined. They stop offering preferences because yours win on warmth. Then you are two specialists arguing across a gap that neither of you is trying to cross any longer. The clean version is a trade that keeps happening. You get better at explaining a want. They get better at admitting one. That is the confrontation doing its real work, which is not to make either of you agree but to leave each of you less partial.
